title: Use independent rheology-state coordinates in the inverse-design objective
quantitative_support: eta80, eta120 and eta80/eta120 are algebraically dependent. V1 uses normalized eta120 and thermal-sensitivity ratio; eta80 remains a hard acceptance window.
claim: The design objective should not triple-count a two-degree-of-freedom temperature response.
limitations: This is a modeling/decision-design result, not experimental evidence.

title: The unconstrained rheology-state optimum is shifted by the formulation boundary
quantitative_support: Global best WO_INV_0419 at NCO/OH=1.7 has MDI fraction 34.06% and fails the 35% floor; the constrained best is WO_INV_0420 at NCO/OH=1.8 with MDI fraction 35.36%.
claim: The final design is a constraint-intersection optimum rather than the unconstrained property optimum.
limitations: Candidate responses are synthetic deterministic benchmark values and require prospective wet-lab validation.

title: Backward reachability predicts the first admissible discrete NCO/OH state
quantitative_support: For the 50/50 PPG700/PPG1000 blend, the continuous 35 wt% MDI threshold is NCO/OH=1.7720; on the 0.1 design grid the first admissible state is 1.8 (WO_INV_0420).
claim: Backward constraint analysis exactly explains why the frozen lab target is NCO/OH=1.8 rather than 1.7.
limitations: Reachability is defined on the frozen candidate manifold and formulation constraints.
